errors.text: The targeted property is misidentified: the hidden target concerns improving coercivity in Fe-Co-Ni-derived fcc high-entropy alloys beyond the approximately 100 Oe single-phase limit, whereas the generated hypothesis focuses on stacking-fault energy.

The central scientific challenge is misidentified: the target concerns explaining how a nominally small orbital moment contributes to enhanced coercivity through dual-phase interactions, spin canting, and domain-wall pinning, not separating orbital contributions to magnetic entropy in longitudinal-spin-fluctuation models.
The generated system is primarily the paramagnetic CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy, while the target is as-cast FeCoNiTi containing coexisting fcc and C14 Laves phases.
The proposed computational intervention omits the target's decisive dual-phase synthesis, C14-dominant comparator, magnetic-transition measurements, and coercivity measurements.

The cited evidence supports effects of longitudinal spin fluctuations on magnetic entropy and stacking-fault energy but provides no evidence that orbital moments significantly control either quantity.
